$comment: Read-differential for the PUBLIC wardrobe READ trio + the shared-archetype
tier: v4's WardrobeRepository.findByCharacterId (-> getOverlaidWardrobeItems)
and findByIdForCharacter (-> findArchetypeById), ported to
quilltap-core::db::wardrobe_read + archetype_wardrobe.
ONE committed file drives BOTH sides. build-wardrobe-public-read-fixture.ts bakes
the SHARED state into two DBs (main + mount-index):
1. A character baked via the REAL repos.characters.create (pinned id + ts), which
mints a linked vault mount + scaffolds an empty Wardrobe/. The builder then reads
the character's minted characterDocumentMountPointId and seeds its Wardrobe/*.md
files there via the REAL linkDocumentContent (NOT writeDatabaseDocument).
2. A provisioned Quilltap General store (doc_mount_points row, pinned id; storeType
'documents', mountType 'database' -- the schema has no 'general' storeType, the
General store is an ordinary documents store whose id lives in
instance_settings.generalMountPointId). Two archetype items seeded into
General/Wardrobe/*.md.
3. Into the character's vault: a plain item, a COMPOSITE whose componentItems refs
one archetype by SLUG and one by UUID (only resolvable via archetype SEEDING), and
an ARCHIVED item (exercises the include-archived filter).
The oracle drives v4's REAL repos.wardrobe over five cases; the Rust test calls the
matching db::wardrobe_read / archetype_wardrobe fns. Both READ the same baked rows so
everything (ids, timestamps, resolved component ids) compares EXACTLY -- ZERO
normalization (no clock mint on a read path).
CASES:
0. findByCharacterId(char, false) -- active items only (archived filtered out).
1. findByCharacterId(char, true)  -- includes the archived item.
2. findByIdForCharacter(char, composite-id) -- owned composite; its componentItemIds
resolved to the two archetype ids (proves seeding: slug + UUID refs land).
3. findByIdForCharacter(char, archetype-A-id) -- NOT owned -> archetype fallback
returns the archetype (characterId null).
4. findByIdForCharacter(char, 'no-such-id') -- null.
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is a THROWAWAY 32-byte key (the same one folders/tags/
characters use). NOT the real Friday pepper; safe to commit.
